title: Rust
subtitle: A systems language that gives you the speed and control of C with memory safety checked by the compiler, from a first program to professional practice.
description: Rust is a compiled systems programming language that reached version 1.0 in 2015. It produces fast native programs with no garbage collector, and its compiler checks rules about ownership and borrowing that rule out whole families of bugs (use-after-free, data races, null dereferences) before a program ever runs. It is used for command-line tools, web services and cloud infrastructure, browsers, operating-system components, embedded devices and WebAssembly.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. It starts with installing Rust and printing a first line, works through the core language and the ownership model that makes Rust different, and ends with error handling, testing, concurrency, the tools professionals use every day, and a complete small project written in idiomatic style.

To run the code, install Rust with the official installer, rustup, from [rust-lang.org/tools/install](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install); it gives you the compiler, Cargo and the standard library. Or try any program in the browser at the [Rust Playground](https://play.rust-lang.org/). Every complete program in these lessons was compiled with the 2024 edition and run by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Install Rust, write and run programs with Cargo, and learn the core language: values and types, control flow and pattern matching, and the ownership and borrowing rules at the heart of Rust.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Model data with structs and enums, abstract with traits and generics, and do everyday work with collections, iterators and closures.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Handle errors and write tests the way Rust teams do, share data safely across threads, know what unsafe code is for, and build a complete project with the everyday tools of the ecosystem.
